summary: R2 completeness review of WP-SCP-023 023B at HEAD commit dd88b2e. All 6 R1 completeness findings (1 MAJ + 5 MIN) are verified closed: CG-MAJ-001 — plan-doc §5 example JSON no longer contains a `signature` field, replaced with an explanatory OIDC-attestation comment (verified by reading plan-doc lines 112–140); CG-MIN-001 — DISPATCH-NOTE OUT section ambiguity resolved in FIX-ROUND-1.md record, distinguishing in-payload Ed25519 signature (correctly OUT) from OIDC attestation (IN as step 4 of 4); CG-MIN-002 — release notes `gh run download` + `gh attestation verify` commands now correctly reference the `scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json` subdirectory (verified lines 77–81 of v1.2.0.md); CG-MIN-003 — DECISIONS.md has D-040 at line 69 and D-041 at line 70, correct ascending order (verified); CG-MIN-004 — STATUS.md now contains a 'Tracked-forward items from WP-SCP-023 023A (plan-doc) + 023B (emitter)' section with TF-023A-001/002 + TF-023B-001/002 (verified lines 195–201); CG-MIN-005 — TF-023B-001 filed at STATUS.md line 199. FIX-ROUND-1.md per-finding table is internally consistent: tally arithmetic is exact (0+3+1+1=5 MAJ; 2+2+5=9 MIN; 2+2+3=7 nit), 10 inline-fix edits map to exactly 7 files, 2 TFs forwarded match STATUS.md entries, smoke-test (21/21 pytest + pre-push wrapper green) is plausible. All 17 DISPATCH-NOTE ACs are in correct end-state: (i)–(vi) verified by direct schema read (no `signature` property; `additionalProperties: false` enforced throughout; waiver-content exclusion enforced by schema description + pytest scan); (vii) 3 fixture pairs confirmed by glob; (viii)+(ix) confirmed by FIX-ROUND-1 smoke test; (x)–(xiv) confirmed by reading DECISIONS.md, STATUS.md, v1.2.0.md; (xv)–(xvii) correctly process-pending. Two new MIN findings arise: CG-R2-MIN-001 (DISPATCH-NOTE IN table still describes the schema as containing 'signature (placeholder)' though the actual schema has no such field — documentation inconsistency in the planning artifact; normative documents are correct) and CG-R2-MIN-002 (release notes 'Workflow permissions delta' describes the OIDC permissions as workflow-level defaults, but after MAJ-SAFE-001's architectural restructure they are job-level only on the `attest-scorecard` job — release notes were not updated to reflect this improvement). Neither constitutes a governance gap in the normative deliverables. R2 completeness fixpoint reached: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ.

findings.claim: The DISPATCH-NOTE IN scope table entry for `schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json` still describes the schema as containing 'signature (placeholder; OIDC attestation is workflow-level, not in-payload)', but the actual implemented schema has NO `signature` property — `additionalProperties: false` at root with no `signature` entry in `properties` or `required`. CG-MAJ-001's inline fix updated the plan-doc §5 example JSON but not the DISPATCH-NOTE IN table.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md IN table line 18 (schema description): '...rule_config_aggregate (disabled_rules + expiring_within_30d), signature (placeholder; OIDC attestation is workflow-level, not in-payload)...'. schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json lines 1–141: `additionalProperties: false` at root; `required` array lists schema_version/emitted_at/scp_version/repo/ref/commit/verdict/rule_counts/waivers_aggregate/rule_config_aggregate only; `properties` object has no `signature` entry. D-041 rationale (DECISIONS.md line 70): 'Verification: GitHub Actions Artifact Attestation (OIDC-based) via `actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.1.0`' with no mention of an in-payload signature field. Schema description field (schemas/scorecard-emit.schema.json line 5): 'no in-payload signature field — platform-level attestation is the trust anchor'.
findings.impact: A future reviewer or the 023C orchestrator reading only the DISPATCH-NOTE IN table would believe the emitted `scorecard-emit.json` includes a `signature` placeholder field. If they then read the actual schema and find no such field, they must cross-reference FIX-ROUND-1.md to understand the discrepancy, adding unnecessary context-retrieval overhead. Risk is LOW because: (1) the plan-doc §5 (the authoritative 023C reference) is correctly updated; (2) the schema, D-041, and release notes are all consistent in describing no in-payload signature; (3) FIX-ROUND-1.md's CG-MAJ-001 closure record explains the change.
findings.mitigation: Following the CG-MIN-001 precedent ('clarified in FIX-ROUND-1.md not DISPATCH-NOTE'), this R2 review record itself serves as the clarification. Alternatively amend DISPATCH-NOTE IN table: replace 'signature (placeholder; OIDC attestation is workflow-level, not in-payload)' with '(no in-payload signature field — OIDC artifact attestation via actions/attest-build-provenance is the trust anchor; see CG-MAJ-001 closure in FIX-ROUND-1.md)'. Not blocking for merge.

findings.claim: The release notes 'Workflow permissions delta' section (docs/releases/v1.2.0.md lines 36–40) states 'The reusable workflow now declares `attestations: write` + `id-token: write` (in addition to the pre-existing `contents: read` + `statuses: write`)' — phrasing that implies workflow-level default permissions. After MAJ-SAFE-001's architectural restructure (FIX-ROUND-1.md inline-fix edit #4), these permissions are declared ONLY at JOB level on the new `attest-scorecard` job (`if: inputs.scorecard-emit`), NOT at the workflow default level. The release notes were written pre-R1 and were not updated by any of the 10 inline fixes.
findings.evidence: docs/releases/v1.2.0.md lines 36–40: 'The reusable workflow now declares `attestations: write` + `id-token: write` (in addition to the pre-existing `contents: read` + `statuses: write`). These permissions are unused by adopters who do NOT opt in (the `attest-build-provenance` action is gated on `inputs.scorecard-emit`)'. FIX-ROUND-1.md MAJ-SAFE-001 inline-fix: 'removed both permissions from workflow level; added new `attest-scorecard` job with job-scoped `attestations: write` + `id-token: write`, `if: inputs.scorecard-emit`, `needs: policy-check`'. FIX-ROUND-1.md inline-fix summary edit #4: '.github/workflows/policy-check.yml: removed workflow-level `attestations: write` + `id-token: write`; added new `attest-scorecard` job with job-scoped permissions (MAJ-SAFE-001)'. No edit in the FIX-ROUND-1 inline-fix summary touches docs/releases/v1.2.0.md for permissions scope correction.
findings.impact: A security auditor reviewing the release notes would see 'the workflow now declares id-token:write' and reasonably interpret this as a workflow-level default that exposes the OIDC token endpoint to ALL steps in the policy-check job for all callers. This contradicts the actual post-fix architecture (job-level, optional job, not executed for non-opt-in runs). The safety claim ('unused by adopters who do NOT opt in') happens to be MORE accurate after MAJ-SAFE-001 than the description implies — permissions are absent entirely for non-opt-in runs — but the phrasing implies a weaker guarantee. Adopter security teams may flag an unnecessary concern.
findings.mitigation: Amend docs/releases/v1.2.0.md 'Workflow permissions delta' section to reflect job-level scope: 'The reusable workflow gains a new `attest-scorecard` job that declares `attestations: write` + `id-token: write` at JOB level (not workflow default level). This job is gated on `if: inputs.scorecard-emit` and runs only for opt-in adopters; non-opt-in runs never trigger the job and never request OIDC tokens. The pre-existing workflow-level permissions (`contents: read` + `statuses: write`) are unchanged.' Not blocking for merge — the actual security posture is BETTER than the release notes describe; the amendment improves accuracy.
